# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c40 P12](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0012)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** a crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with prominent blue eyes and a round face. He has a small fringe of hair around his ears, which he keeps carefully trimmed when spruced up, and he is very sensitive about his baldness.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

Extremely blunt, hot-tempered, and prone to sudden outbursts of wrath, Mr. Harrison prides himself on being brutally outspoken and telling the plain truth. Despite his crusty, crabbed, and fidgety exterior, he possesses a soft and friendly side, enjoying pleasant company and harboring a fondness for young people. He is deeply sensitive about his baldness and sensitive to pity, often expressing his opinions through dry irony and humor.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c30 P5](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0005)_

## History

Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick, quickly earning a reputation as an eccentric crank who kept irregular domestic habits. He initially clashed with Anne Shirley after finding her Jersey cow in his oat field, but after Anne mistakenly sold his cow and brought him a homemade cake as a peace offering, the two became close friends. When lightning struck his house and killed his troublesome parrot Ginger, Anne came to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea following a comedic misunderstanding involving a published newspaper joke, leading the pair to reconcile and restore order to his household. Mr. Harrison remained a supportive friend and literary critic for Anne during her writing endeavors, providing pragmatic advice on her stories.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c2 P35](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0035), [v2 c2 P42](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0042), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c24 P41](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0041), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c25 P9](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0009), [v2 c25 P14](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0014), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P50](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0050), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P74](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0074)_

## Background by volume

- Moved from New Brunswick to Avonlea in April to buy Robert Bell's farm  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily due to domestic disagreements before moving to Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c25 P43](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0043), [v2 c25 P54](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0054), [v2 c25 P56](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0056)</sub>
- Was frequently whipped by his schoolmaster during his schooldays  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
- Had a brother who was a sailor and gave him a swearing parrot named Ginger  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> So I do . . . so I do . . . but my approval doesn’t go as deep as my pocket, Anne.  <sub>[v2 c6 P59](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0059)</sub>

> Poor Ginger won’t call you any more names, Anne,  <sub>[v2 c24 P44](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0044)</sub>

> Changes ain’t totally pleasant but they’re excellent things. Two years is about long enough for things to stay exactly the same. If they stayed put any longer they might grow mossy.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>

> I’d write a story once in a while, but I wouldn’t pester editors with it. I’d write of people and places like I knew, and I’d make my characters talk everyday English; and I’d let the sun rise and set in the usual quiet way without much fuss over the fact.  <sub>[v3 c12 P74](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0074)</sub>
